title: Loan vs Consortium
description: Compare loan and consortium side by side. See which option leaves more money in your pocket.

property.title: Property value
property.note: This value will be used for both scenarios

rent.title: Rent Income (Optional)
rent.description: If you plan to rent out the property, enter the monthly rent you expect to receive. Loan receives rent from month 1; consortium from contemplation.

investment.title: Invest the difference
investment.note: The monthly difference between installments will be invested at this rate

annualPropertyAppreciation.label: Annual property appreciation
annualPropertyAppreciation.help: Estimated annual property appreciation. Used to calculate loan IRR.

annualAdjustment.label: Annual adjustment (INCC/IPCA)
annualAdjustment.help: Consortium installments are adjusted annually by an index such as INCC or IPCA.

bidAmount.label: Bid amount
bidAmount.help: Amount paid in the contemplation month to anticipate installments. Reduces the outstanding balance and term, saving on admin fees.

contemplationMonth.label: Contemplation month
contemplationMonth.help: Month when you'll be contemplated and receive the credit letter to buy the property. Before that, you pay installments but don't have the asset.

premium.label: Premium for a contemplated letter
premium.help: Amount paid to buy a consortium letter already contemplated. This is added to the initial payment (month 1) and does not change the letter value nor monthly installments.

monthlyRent.label: Monthly rent
monthlyRent.help: Monthly rent you will receive by renting out the property (month 1). This value is treated as monthly income.

annualRentAdjustment.label: Annual adjustment (IGPM)
annualRentAdjustment.help: Annual rent adjustment (typically IGPM). Applied every 12 months (month 13, 25, ...).

annualReturnRate.label: Annual return rate
annualReturnRate.help: Annual return rate you could get by investing the difference between installments. Examples: CDI (~10%), Selic bonds (~10%), CDB (~12%).

lanceAgioError.title: Error:
lanceAgioError.message: Fill in only one of the fields: Bid amount or Premium. These scenarios are mutually exclusive.

lanceAgioNote.title: Note:
lanceAgioNote.message: Bid and Premium are different scenarios. Use bid if you'll be contemplated via draw/bid. Use premium if you're buying a letter already contemplated from a third party.

seo.metaTitle: Loan vs Consortium Comparator | Which is Better?
seo.metaDescription: Compare loan and consortium side by side. See which option leaves more money in your pocket considering interest, admin fees, difference investment, and rent income.

howToUse.title: How to use the comparator
howToUse.step1: Enter the property value that will be used for both scenarios
howToUse.step2: Fill in loan data: down payment, interest rate, term, and amortization system (SAC or Price)
howToUse.step3: Fill in consortium data: term, admin fee, annual adjustment, and contemplation (bid or premium)
howToUse.step4: Optionally, add rent income and return rate for investing the difference
howToUse.step5: Click 'Compare' to see which option is more financially advantageous
howToUse.step6: Analyze net cost, IRR, and accumulated investment balance in each scenario

whyCompare.title: Why compare loan and consortium?
whyCompare.p1: Loan and consortium are two different ways to acquire a property, each with its advantages and disadvantages. The best option depends on your profile, time needs, and financial conditions.
whyCompare.p2: Comparing both options side by side allows you to make a more informed decision, considering not only total cost, but also factors like liquidity, flexibility, and opportunity to invest the difference between installments.
whyCompare.p3: This calculator considers all relevant factors: loan interest, consortium admin fee, monthly difference investment, rent income, and property appreciation.

keyDifferences.title: Key differences between loan and consortium
keyDifferences.intro: Understand the characteristics of each modality:

financiamento.title: Loan
financiamento.p1: Has interest: you pay interest on the financed amount
financiamento.p2: Receive the property immediately after approval
financiamento.p3: Installments can vary (SAC) or be fixed (Price)
financiamento.p4: Can make extra amortizations to reduce interest
financiamento.p5: Total cost depends on interest rate and term

consorcio.title: Consortium
consorcio.p2: Need to wait for contemplation (lottery or bid)
consorcio.p3: Installments are adjusted annually by INCC/IPCA
consorcio.p4: Can give a bid to anticipate contemplation
consorcio.p5: Total cost depends on admin fee and annual adjustment

totalCost.title: How to calculate total cost
totalCost.intro: The total cost of each option is calculated considering all payments:
totalCost.financiamentoFormula: Loan: Total paid = Down payment + Sum of all installments + Interest paid
totalCost.consorcioFormula: Consortium: Total paid = Down payment (if any) + Premium (if buying contemplated letter) + Sum of all installments + Admin fee
totalCost.note: The calculator also considers investing the monthly difference between installments, showing the final net cost when you invest the difference at a return rate.

investmentDifference.title: Investing the monthly difference
investmentDifference.intro: An important advantage of comparing both options is considering what to do with the difference between installments:
investmentDifference.example: If the loan costs R$ 3,000/month and the consortium costs R$ 2,500/month, you have R$ 500/month difference. If you invest this difference at 10% per year, by the end of the term you'll have accumulated a significant amount that reduces the loan's net cost.
investmentDifference.note: The calculator shows the accumulated investment balance month by month, allowing you to see how investing the difference impacts the final net cost of each option.

whenToChoose.title: When to choose each option
whenToChoose.intro: The best choice depends on your profile and needs:

financiamento.title: Choose loan when:
financiamento.c1: You need the property immediately (without waiting for contemplation)
financiamento.c2: Interest rate is competitive and you can make extra amortizations
financiamento.c3: You prefer more predictable installments and want control over the term

consorcio.title: Choose consortium when:
consorcio.c1: You can wait for contemplation or have conditions to give a bid
consorcio.c2: Admin fee is lower than loan interest
consorcio.c3: You prefer no interest and are willing to deal with annual adjustment

example.title: Practical example
example.s2: Loan: 10% per year, 180 months, SAC, R$ 100,000 down payment
example.s3: Consortium: 15% admin fee, 180 months, contemplation month 12 with R$ 20,000 bid

example.w2: IRR: see which option has better return considering future property value
example.w3: Monthly evolution: observe when each option becomes cheaper over time
example.w4: Investment balance: see how much you accumulate investing the difference between installments

disclaimer.title: Important notice
disclaimer.text: This calculator is educational and provides estimates based on entered data. Results may vary due to factors such as changes in interest rates, specific contract conditions, additional costs not considered (insurance, fees, taxes), and market variations. Use results as an analysis tool and consult financial professionals for important decisions.

q1.question: Which is better: loan or consortium?
q1.answer: It depends on your profile and needs. Loan is better if you need the property immediately and can get a good interest rate. Consortium is better if you can wait for contemplation and the admin fee is lower than loan interest. Use this calculator to compare specific scenarios.

q2.question: How does investing the difference work?
q2.answer: When one option has a lower installment than the other, the monthly difference can be invested. For example, if the loan costs R$ 3,000 and the consortium R$ 2,500, you invest R$ 500/month. By the end, this accumulated investment reduces the net cost of the more expensive option, making the comparison fairer.

q3.question: What is net cost?
q3.answer: Net cost is total paid minus income (rent) and minus accumulated investment balance. It's the most important metric to compare both options, as it considers all cash flows: payments, income, and investments.

q4.question: Why is rent considered in the comparison?
q4.answer: If you plan to rent the property, rent income reduces the net cost of both options. In a loan, you receive rent from month 1. In a consortium, you only receive after contemplation (when you have the property). This significantly impacts the comparison.

q5.question: How to interpret IRR in the comparison?
q5.answer: IRR (Internal Rate of Return) shows the financial return of each option considering the future property value. A higher IRR indicates better return. Compare loan and consortium IRRs to see which generates better return on investment.

q6.question: What to do if the result shows a technical tie?
q6.answer: If net cost is practically equal, consider other factors: time need (loan is immediate, consortium needs waiting), flexibility (loan allows extra amortizations), and personal preference. The difference may be so small that other factors become decisive.

q7.question: Does the calculator consider all costs?
q7.answer: The calculator considers main costs: interest, admin fee, annual adjustment, and difference investment. It doesn't necessarily include all costs like insurance, contract fees, taxes, and other specific expenses. Use as an estimate and validate with real proposals from banks and administrators.
